41: 	newPath := make(cty.Path, len(path), len(path)+len(nextSteps))

15: // filterMarks removes any PathValueMarks from marks which cannot be applied to
16: // the given value. When comparing existing marks to those from a map or other
17: // dynamic value, we may not have values at the same paths and need to strip
18: // out irrelevant marks.
19: func filterMarks(val cty.Value, marks []cty.PathValueMarks) []cty.PathValueMarks {
20: 	var res []cty.PathValueMarks
21: 	for _, mark := range marks {
22: 		// any error here just means the path cannot apply to this value, so we
23: 		// don't need this mark for comparison.
24: 		if _, err := mark.Path.Apply(val); err == nil {
25: 			res = append(res, mark)

27: 	}
28: 	return res
29: }

32: // the comparison using the cty.PathValueMarks.Equal method.
33: func marksEqual(a, b []cty.PathValueMarks) bool {
34: 	if len(a) == 0 && len(b) == 0 {
35: 		return true
36: 	}
37: 
38: 	if len(a) != len(b) {
39: 		return false
40: 	}
41: 
42: 	less := func(s []cty.PathValueMarks) func(i, j int) bool {
43: 		return func(i, j int) bool {
44: 			// the sort only needs to be consistent, so use the GoString format
45: 			// to get a comparable value
46: 			return fmt.Sprintf("%#v", s[i]) < fmt.Sprintf("%#v", s[j])
47: 		}
48: 	}
49: 
50: 	sort.Slice(a, less(a))
51: 	sort.Slice(b, less(b))
52: 
53: 	for i := 0; i < len(a); i++ {
54: 		if !a[i].Equal(b[i]) {
55: 			return false
56: 		}
57: 	}

64: // will be duplicates from a prior value already in the list of marks. While

67: func dedupePathValueMarks(m []cty.PathValueMarks) []cty.PathValueMarks {
68: 	var res []cty.PathValueMarks

70: 	// the Path portion is not automagically comparable.

77: 		}
78: 		seen[key] = true
79: 		res = append(res, pvm)
80: 	}

82: 	return res
83: }
